facts.AUS: Sydney and Melbourne both wanted to be the capital, so Canberra was built from scratch in between as a compromise.
facts.CAN: Ottawa was picked by Queen Victoria in 1857, partly as a compromise between English- and French-speaking Canada.
facts.USA: Washington, D.C. isn't part of any state: D.C. stands for District of Columbia.
facts.TUR: Istanbul is far bigger, but Atatürk made Ankara the capital in 1923.
facts.BRA: Brasília was built from nothing in the interior and opened in 1960, taking over from Rio de Janeiro.
facts.CHE: Switzerland has no official capital by law. Bern is the 'federal city' where the government sits.
facts.NZL: Wellington is the southernmost capital of any sovereign country. Auckland is bigger.
facts.NGA: Abuja replaced Lagos in 1991, chosen for its central, neutral location.
facts.PAK: Islamabad was purpose-built in the 1960s, replacing Karachi.
facts.MAR: Rabat is the capital; Casablanca is the biggest city.
facts.VNM: Hanoi is in the north; Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) in the south is bigger.
facts.IND: New Delhi is part of the much bigger city of Delhi.
facts.KAZ: Astana replaced Almaty as capital in 1997. It was called Nur-Sultan from 2019 to 2022.
facts.TZA: Dodoma is the official capital, but Dar es Salaam is far bigger and still the main business hub.
facts.CMR: Yaoundé is the capital; the port city of Douala is bigger.
facts.MMR: Naypyidaw was built in secret and made the capital in 2005, replacing Yangon.
facts.ZAF: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria (government), Cape Town (parliament) and Bloemfontein (courts). Any of them counts.
facts.BOL: Sucre is the constitutional capital, but the government sits in La Paz (both count). At about 3,600 m, La Paz is the highest seat of government in the world.
facts.ECU: Quito sits at about 2,850 m, only around 25 km from the equator.
facts.ARE: Abu Dhabi is the capital; Dubai is the bigger, more famous city.
facts.SAU: Riyadh is the capital, in the middle of the country.
facts.ISR: Israel names Jerusalem as its capital, but this is disputed internationally, and many countries keep their embassies in Tel Aviv.
facts.PSE: Palestine claims East Jerusalem as its capital; its government works from Ramallah. Both count.
facts.BDI: Gitega became the political capital in 2019. Bujumbura is still the biggest city.
facts.CIV: Yamoussoukro, hometown of the first president, has been the official capital since 1983. It has a basilica modelled on St Peter's in Rome. Abidjan, where most government work happens, counts too.
facts.BEN: Porto-Novo is the official capital, but the government mostly sits in Cotonou. Both count.
facts.NLD: Amsterdam is the capital by the constitution, but the government, parliament and king work in The Hague. Both count.
facts.MYS: Kuala Lumpur is the official capital, but the government moved to the planned city of Putrajaya. Both count.
facts.LKA: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is the official capital, right next to Colombo, the commercial capital. Both count.
facts.MLT: Valletta is the smallest capital in the European Union.
facts.PLW: Ngerulmud has been the capital since 2006. It's one of the least populated capitals in the world.
facts.BLZ: Belmopan was built inland after Hurricane Hattie wrecked Belize City in 1961.
facts.MWI: Lilongwe replaced Zomba as capital in 1975. Blantyre is the main business city.
facts.BTN: Thimphu famously has no traffic lights; police officers direct traffic instead.
facts.MNG: Ulaanbaatar is the coldest capital city in the world.
facts.ISL: Reykjavík is the northernmost capital of a sovereign country.
facts.GRL: Nuuk is slightly further north than Reykjavík.
facts.NOR: Oslo was called Christiania (later Kristiania) until 1925.
facts.IDN: Jakarta is sinking and crowded, so a new capital, Nusantara, is being built on Borneo.
facts.DEU: Bonn was West Germany's capital. Berlin became the capital again after reunification in 1990.
facts.VAT: Vatican City is a city-state entirely surrounded by Rome.
facts.KOR: About half of South Korea's population lives in and around Seoul.
facts.JPN: Kyoto was Japan's imperial capital for over a thousand years before Tokyo.
facts.THA: Bangkok's full ceremonial name is one of the longest place names in the world. Thais call it Krung Thep.
facts.POL: Kraków was the capital until around 1596, when the king moved to Warsaw.
facts.SVK: Bratislava is the only national capital that borders two other countries: Austria and Hungary.
facts.HUN: Budapest was formed in 1873 by joining Buda, Óbuda and Pest.
facts.ARM: Yerevan was founded in 782 BC, which makes it older than Rome.
facts.AZE: Baku lies about 28 m below sea level, the lowest national capital in the world.
facts.TKM: Ashgabat holds a world record for the most white marble buildings.
facts.TJK: Dushanbe means 'Monday' in Tajik, after a Monday market held there.
facts.ETH: Addis Ababa means 'new flower' and is home to the African Union.
facts.SDN: Khartoum is where the Blue Nile and the White Nile meet.
facts.SEN: Dakar is the westernmost city of mainland Africa.
facts.COD: Kinshasa and Brazzaville (capital of the Republic of the Congo) face each other across the Congo River. Apart from Rome and Vatican City, they're the closest capitals in the world.
facts.COG: Brazzaville and Kinshasa (capital of DR Congo) face each other across the Congo River. Apart from Rome and Vatican City, they're the closest capitals in the world.
facts.MOZ: Maputo was called Lourenço Marques until 1976.
facts.DOM: Santo Domingo is the oldest European-founded city in the Americas still standing (1496).
facts.HND: Tegucigalpa's name is often said to mean 'silver hills' in an indigenous language.
facts.MNE: Podgorica is the capital, but the constitution names Cetinje the 'Old Royal Capital'.
facts.PHL: Manila is the capital, part of the huge Metro Manila area, which also includes Quezon City.
facts.RUS: Saint Petersburg was Russia's capital for about 200 years before Moscow took over again in 1918.
facts.ITA: Rome is nicknamed 'the Eternal City'. Milan is Italy's business capital.
facts.ESP: Madrid was chosen partly because it sits right in the middle of the country.
facts.EGY: Cairo is one of the largest cities in Africa. Alexandria was Egypt's capital in ancient times.
facts.GNQ: Malabo is on an island, not the mainland. A new capital, Ciudad de la Paz, is being built on the mainland.
facts.GMB: Banjul is on an island at the mouth of the Gambia River.
facts.PER: Lima was founded by the Spanish conquistador Francisco Pizarro in 1535.
facts.ARG: Buenos Aires means 'good airs' or 'fair winds'.
facts.SGP: Singapore is a city-state: the city and the country are the same.
facts.MCO: Monaco is a city-state and the second-smallest country in the world, after Vatican City.
facts.LUX: Luxembourg City shares its name with the country. Its old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.KWT: Kuwait City is home to most of Kuwait's population.
facts.FIN: Helsinki took over from Turku as capital in 1812, under Russian rule.
facts.IRL: Dublin comes from the Irish 'Dubh Linn', meaning 'black pool'.
facts.GBR: London has been a major city since the Romans founded it as Londinium.
facts.NPL: Kathmandu sits in a valley at about 1,400 m in the Himalayas.
facts.AFG: Kabul lies at about 1,800 m, one of the highest capitals in the world.
facts.BRN: Bandar Seri Begawan is named after Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien III, father of the current sultan.
facts.FRO: Tórshavn, 'Thor's harbour', is one of the smallest capitals in the world.
facts.XKX: Pristina is also spelled Prishtina. Both count.
facts.TWN: Taipei 101 was the world's tallest building from 2004 to 2010.
facts.ESH: Laayoune (El Aaiún) is controlled by Morocco; Western Sahara's status is disputed.
